title: Coherent restriction of relative right Kan extensions
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and full subcategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and relative limit diagrams and join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Work in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow C$ be a full subcategory of a small quasicategory, let $p:D\to B$ be an isofibration of quasicategories, and let $s:C\to B$ be a functor. Here an isofibration is an inner fibration as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] which lifts each equivalence to an equivalence with any prescribed source. Put $\operatorname{Fun}_s(C,D)=\operatorname{Fun}(C,D)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,B)}\{s\}$, the degreewise fiber, and define $\operatorname{Fun}_{sj}(A,D)$ similarly. For $c\in C$ put $J_c=A\times_C C_{c/}$, using simplices starting at $c$ and their entire remaining face, and let $l_c:J_c^{\triangleleft}\to C$ be its canonical cone. A functor $H\in\operatorname{Fun}_s(C,D)$ is $p$-right Kan extended from $A$ when $Hl_c$ is a $p$-limit diagram for every $c$. Let $\mathcal K$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_s(C,D)$ on these functors. Assume that every $h\in\operatorname{Fun}_{sj}(A,D)$ has such an extension $H$ with $Hj=h$ exactly. Then restriction $j^*:\mathcal K\to\operatorname{Fun}_{sj}(A,D)$ is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets: it has the right lifting property for every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$, $r\geq0$. In particular restriction is an equivalence of infinity categories and induces natural equivalences of their mapping spaces. Thus extensions of diagrams, transformations and higher parameter simplices with any already prescribed compatible boundary exist coherently; no global completeness assumption on $D$ or on the fibers of $p$ is imposed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory Proposition 4.3.2.15 and Remark 4.3.2.18 (right-hand dual), printed pp. 284-285, conditional on existence for every boundary diagram; Lemma 4.3.2.12 for coherent restriction. Read online; archive WANTED. This is HTT, not Higher Algebra. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: First check the categories in the assertion. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\varnothing\subseteq C$ and $\varnothing\subseteq A$: postcomposition by $p$ on each functor category is an isofibration. Each strict fiber over $s$ or $sj$ is a quasicategory, since an inner horn in that fiber is filled by the inner-fibration lifting property over the constant simplex at the specified base diagram. Its filler remains in the fiber. The full subcategory $\mathcal K$ is a quasicategory: $\operatorname{Fun}(C,D)$ is one by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], an inner horn in $\mathcal K$ has a filler in the fiber $\operatorname{Fun}_s(C,D)$ as just shown, and the filler has the same vertices, so lies in $\mathcal K$ by fullness. Restriction preserves the defining strict base equation.

source.place: Preparations for Proposition 4.3.2.15; strict functor fibers and full subcategories

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] to the same $A\subseteq C$, $p:D\to B$ and $s$; its $L_c$, $a_c$, $l_c$ are the item's $J_c$, the projection $J_c\to A$, and $l_c$ (simplices starting at $c$, projected by their entire final face), and its $\operatorname{Fun}_s(C,D)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{s|_A}(A,D)$ are the item's degreewise fibers. Its full subcategory $R$ of pointwise $p$-right Kan extensions is exactly $\mathcal K$. Its full subcategory $T$ is all of $\operatorname{Fun}_{sj}(A,D)$: for a vertex $h$, the assumed extension $H$ with $Hj=h$ gives the cone $Hl_c:J_c^{\triangleleft}\to D$, which is a $p$-limit diagram, satisfies $Hl_c|_{J_c}=Hja_c=ha_c$ because $l_c|_{J_c}=ja_c$, and satisfies $pHl_c=sl_c$ because $pH=s$. A full subcategory on every object is the whole simplicial set. Hence that node's conclusion is that $j^*:\mathcal K\to\operatorname{Fun}_{sj}(A,D)$ is a trivial Kan fibration, i.e. has the right lifting property for every $\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$, $r\geq0$; in dimension zero this lift is the assumed extension. Since $\partial\Delta^0$ is empty, the dimension-zero clause is surjectivity on vertices, so this is a trivial Kan fibration in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. In particular extensions of diagrams, transformations and higher simplices with prescribed compatible boundary exist exactly.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.2.15 and Remark 4.3.2.18 (right-hand dual), printed pp. 284-285, specialized to the case where every diagram on A admits the local relative limit cones

proof.text: Finally [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] shows that this restriction map lifts every degreewise injective map. The cofibrations in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] are exactly those maps; its weak factorization system therefore makes restriction a Joyal trivial fibration and hence a categorical equivalence. Both its source and target are quasicategories by step 1, so [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], clause (2), makes it a functor equivalence. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it induces equivalences on all mapping spaces. The map on these spaces is the one induced by restriction itself: composition with restriction commutes with restriction of simplices, so the comparison is natural in both arguments and retains the coherent composition data. Only the assumed extensions of objects, through the local cones they supply in step 2, have been used; no completeness hypothesis was added.

source.place: Consequence of Proposition 4.3.2.15 and Remark 4.3.2.18; categorical-equivalence interpretation

proof_origin.place: Special case of the right-hand dual of HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15 (Remark 4.3.2.18), through the existing node lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction, whose T is the whole fiber under the item's existence hypothesis; categorical-equivalence and mapping-space consequences through the Joyal model structure. The three helper definitions belong to this restriction statement; no notion is duplicated or arbitrary map chosen. The conclusion includes quasicategory closure, all boundary lifts (including dimension zero), coherent functor equivalence and the actual induced mapping-space equivalences.
